gemini.rationale: The slice explicitly notes that the party contributing the solar-cell technology and process know-how (SPTL) is not the party that nominates the operating chief executive of the manufacturing entity (AUO), creating a structural mismatch between the operational processes and the management running them (gap_56). This gap is mitigated at closing by licensing and joint-development agreements, a shared board, and deadlock-resolution mechanisms.

grok.rationale: gap_45 is 0 because at closing the JVC both manufactures the customer-facing product (solar cells sold cost-plus to SPSW and AUO) and receives the producing processes alongside it: SPTL and AUO each license background IP into the JVC and the venture is to deploy SunPower cell technology/process know-how together with AUO manufacturing expertise to install and operate Fab 3. gap_56 is 1 because the same closing instruments assign process/technology contribution to SPTL while giving AUO the right to nominate the JVC CEO (SPTL nominates only the CFO), a documented process-vs-operating-organization mismatch; that gap is contractually absorbed at closing by the royalty-free cross-licenses, joint-development agreements, seven-year supply agreements, and 50/50 board governance.

openai.rationale: The solar cells and their producing processes were colocated in the JVC: it would manufacture and sell the cells using SunPower technology and process know-how together with AUO manufacturing expertise, governed by royalty-free licenses and joint-development arrangements [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-10-129898, Form 8-K Item 1.01]. Although the technology contributor and CEO nominator differed, the operating organization was coherently allocated at closing through a shared board, AUO's CEO nomination right, and SPTL's CFO nomination right, so no process-versus-organization gap is documented [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-10-129898, Form 8-K Item 1.01].
